metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness records per-call token use and terminal quota failures, but it does not expose a live subscription quota window or burndown percentage.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: no
daemon_capability: n/a
driver_capability: ready

## Scenario signal

The scenario requires one subscription session to expose a fresh `RateLimitSnapshot` after each turn. The snapshot must contain a quota window whose `UsedPercent` does not decrease, and `SampledAt` must advance. Per-call token counts and terminal quota failures do not satisfy this signal.

## Agent capability

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 does not expose the required live quota-window signal. The required `strings` scan of the installed `dsh` launcher returned no match for quota, rate limit, used percent, subscription, balance, or usage. A separate scan of the installed official packages found terminal `QUOTA` and `RATE_LIMIT` error classes, but no quota-window, used-percent, reset-time, or subscription-plan record. Those error classes describe a failed request after a limit is reached. They do not report progressive consumption before exhaustion.

The installed durable-session schema confirms the boundary. `SessionEventMap` persists lifecycle, messages, tools, request context, and assistant usage. The complete `TokenUsage` type contains input, output, total, cache-read, cache-write, and reasoning token counts only. It has no plan, quota window, used percent, remaining amount, or reset time. A measured v3 transcript from the configured LM Studio route contains provider, model, context window, and one positive token-usage vector. A full quota-carrier scan of that decoded transcript returned no match.

The current recording driver makes the environment constraint explicit. It replaces the default provider route with local LM Studio at `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` and selects `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`. This local route has no subscription account or provider quota window for DSH to expose. The agent therefore lacks the behavior that this scenario tests.

## Daemon capability

Daemon capability is `n/a` because the agent does not emit the required feature. The DSH adapter tails the compressed v3 session log. Its parser handles lifecycle, messages, tools, model, context-window, and token-usage records. `parseAssistantUsage` maps only input, output, and total tokens. No record handler or parser path creates a `RateLimitSnapshot`. That absence matches the trace that DSH writes and is not a daemon bug.

## Driver capability and route

The driver is `ready` by the frozen-no-feature convention. Its declared primitives include `send`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`, which would be enough for a three-turn recipe if the agent emitted quota snapshots. No driver primitive can create a missing agent-owned quota signal. The recipe is therefore `applicable:false`, and the route is `frozen`.

## Vacuous-pass check

This cell could pass while proving no burndown because its frozen meta-only spec launches no session and observes no turns. That is intentional for a capability-absence claim. Reassess after a DSH upgrade or recording-route change only if the durable log gains a plan, quota-window, used-percent, remaining-quota, or reset-time carrier.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: the frozen meta-only spec passes without launching DSH or observing multiple turns. It documents a capability-absence claim and does not test runtime burndown.

Load-bearing environment precondition: the current driver pins a self-hosted LM Studio route and qwen/qwen3.5-9b. That route has no subscription account. Reassess if the driver changes to a provider-authenticated subscription route and DSH persists its quota window.
DSH `QUOTA` and `RATE_LIMIT` error classes are terminal request-failure facts. They do not supply the pre-exhaustion `UsedPercent` and fresh `SampledAt` values required by this scenario.
The capability scan covers DSH 0.1.5-rc.2. Re-run the launcher, installed-package, durable-schema, and transcript scans after an agent upgrade.

recipe.notes: Frozen on agent_supports=no. DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 persists per-call token usage and terminal quota errors, but no subscription quota window, used percent, remaining quota, or reset time. Reassess only after DSH persists a progressive quota carrier.
